deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and no derivations. It holds two reading excerpts in Riemann's hand, the kind of notes he kept while studying Herbartian philosophy.

(1) A citation and paraphrase from Fichte's 'Zeitschrift für Philosophie und philosophische Kritik', vol. XXI, p. 37, in a contribution by M. W. Drobisch. The left-margin heading 'Fichte' refers to the editor of the journal, I. H. Fichte. The excerpt says that Herbart's 'Methode der Beziehungen' (method of relations) essentially coincides with Herbart's theory of ground and consequence (Grund und Folge). In that form it permits a simpler [or 'surer'] and more natural presentation. Riemann adds a cross-reference to Drobisch, 'Neue Darstellung der Logik', 2nd ed. (1851), §§ 136 and 138.

(2) A verbatim extract from Leibniz's 'Nouveaux Essais sur l'entendement humain' in the German translation by Ulrich (Leibniz, 'Neue Versuche über den menschlichen Verstand', transl. J. H. F. Ulrich, Halle 1778–80), vol. I, p. 136. It comes from Book I, the polemic on innate ideas. Theophilus grants that Locke ('the learned author of the Essay') rightly noticed a gross abuse. People shelter their own prejudices under the name of innate ideas to avoid the labour of examining them. Locke's hostility to the doctrine is therefore aimed at intellectual laziness, not at innateness properly understood. Such people claim that nature engraved certain notions and truths in the soul. On that pretext they stop investigating the sources, connections and certainty of such knowledge.

The page is relevant to Riemann's documented philosophical interests: Herbart's psychology and metaphysics, the theory of concepts, and Leibniz on the origin of knowledge. It belongs to the background of his Naturphilosophie fragments and of the epistemological remarks in his Habilitationsvortrag. There is nothing to compute.

results.what: Excerpt noting that Herbart's 'method of relations' coincides with his theory of ground and consequence (after Drobisch).
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Herbart; M. W. Drobisch (commentary, c. 1850s)

results.what: Quotation from Leibniz's Nouveaux Essais (German transl. by Ulrich) on the abuse of the doctrine of innate ideas.

deep.surprise_reason: These are purely bibliographic and philosophical reading notes with no mathematical content. Riemann's study of Herbart (and Drobisch) and his interest in Leibniz are well documented, e.g. by E. Scholz (1982) and in the Werke 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'eine sicherere[?] und natürlichere Darstellung' — the image more plausibly reads 'eine einfachere und natürlichere Darstellung'.
Top-left marginal word, read as 'Fichte[?]', is the underlined heading 'Fichte' (the journal's editor), placed before 'Zeitschrift f. Ph. & phil. Kritik'.
Line 5: the closing parenthesis after '§. 136 & 138.' is missing in the manuscript itself; this is not a transcription error.
Marginal heading of the second excerpt: 'Leibniz' is underlined in the original.
